text:
alice (Support): Hey team — customer reported duplicate charges after a sequence of 429s + retries. They say their client used the SDK defaults. Posting logs: 

alice (Support): 2024-08-15T10:02:31Z -> POST /v1/generate 429, x-request-id=abc123, retry-after=1
alice (Support): 2024-08-15T10:02:32Z -> SDK retry #1 -> 200 (charged) x-request-id=def456
alice (Support): 2024-08-15T10:02:32Z -> SDK retry #2 -> 200 (charged again) x-request-id=ghi789

alice (Support): Customer says they used default SDK settings (node). They didn't set idempotency-key. Ticket attached: INC-8723. They want: (1) why did SDK retry twice in <1s, (2) how to avoid duplicate billing, (3) what server-side dedupe exists? @kevin @diego

kevin (SDK): thanks for the report, alice. quick answers up front: (a) SDK default tries fast retries to favor latency-sensitive UX unless configured otherwise, (b) without an idempotency key the server treats each request independently so two successful responses => two billable events, (c) we should recommend customers set an idempotency-key header or enable "strictIdempotency" in the SDK for charge-type endpoints. :+1:

kevin (SDK): SDK defaults (node 1.4.x) we ship: maxRetries: 3, backoff: linear with baseDelay=100ms, respectRetryAfter: true but only when Retry-After parsed; jitter is small. That makes a fast second attempt if Retry-After header is low or missing. For high-throughput clients this can amplify bursts.

kevin (SDK): Recommended config for production: exponential backoff with full jitter, reduce maxRetries to 2 for non-idempotent endpoints, and always send idempotency-key for operations that create charges. Example (pseudo):

kevin (SDK): ```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  retry: {
    maxRetries: 2,
    strategy: 'expo-jitter',
    baseDelayMs: 200,
    maxDelayMs: 5000,
    respectRetryAfter: true
  },
  defaults: { strictIdempotency: false }
});

// customer should set their own idempotency key on create calls:
await client.post('/v1/charge', { amount: 1000 }, { headers: { 'Idempotency-Key': userTxnId } });
```

kevin (SDK): If they prefer SDK to auto-generate keys, enable strictIdempotency=true so the SDK will populate and retry-suppress, but recommend customers still provide a business key for cross-process dedupe.

diego (Infra): server-side notes: our quota/rate limiter is a token-bucket per-project with short burst allowance (burstTokens ~= 5 * normal rate) to avoid breaking steady small spikes. But when token bucket is exhausted we return 429. We do not automatically dedupe arbitrary POSTs unless an Idempotency-Key is present and the endpoint is configured for idempotency (payments, async jobs). For these endpoints we dedupe using (project, endpoint, idempotency-key) for a 24h window. If no key -> each successful request accepted and billed.

diego (Infra): Also important: if client retries while the original request is still pending server-side (race), the backend might process both if idempotency isn't provided. The x-request-id you posted shows three different request IDs — that's consistent with 3 distinct processed requests.

lina (AccountOps): On billing side: if the customer shows clear repro and duplicate charges within the same minute due to retries we can issue a credit while they remediate. For us to process a refund quickly we need: project id, customer txn id, timestamps, and the three x-request-ids (abc123/def456/ghi789). Send to billing@redwood with INC number.

kevin (SDK): For immediate mitigation advise customer to: 1) set Idempotency-Key per business txn, 2) change SDK retry strategy to expo+jitter and lower maxRetries, 3) respect Retry-After and back off longer on 429s, 4) add client-side circuit breaker (open if 5 consecutive 429s in 60s).

alice (Support): @kevin can you share a quick curl example they can paste?

kevin (SDK): sure — this will attach an idempotency header: 

kevin (SDK): ```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/charge \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: order_12345_us-east-1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"amount":1000, "currency":"usd"}'
```

kevin (SDK): Also show them how to enable expo+jitter in node config: 

kevin (SDK): ```js
// example using new SDK config
client.setRetryPolicy({
  maxRetries: 2,
  algorithm: 'expo-jitter',
  baseMs: 300,
  maxMs: 4000
});
```

diego (Infra): one additional server optimization in rollout: we recently added stronger 429 Retry-After headers on per-route limits (some customers might still see old behavior while infra rolls out). If Retry-After present the SDK should honour it; if missing treat 429 as a sign of quota and back off more aggressively.

alice (Support): customer also asked whether SDK default should change — they were surprised by linear fast retries. Thoughts?

kevin (SDK): We're planning a defaults update in next minor: expo-jitter and higher baseDelay for non-idempotent endpoints, plus a feature flag to auto-insert idempotency keys for create endpoints when the caller opts in. We'll add clearer docs and a migration guide.

lina (AccountOps): I'll take the refund/credit request once alice collects the IDs. Also we can flag the account to prevent future automated billings during their remediation window.

alice (Support): I'll reply to the customer with the curl example, recommended SDK settings, and request the x-request-ids/timestamps. I'll also offer a temporary credit while they fix their client. Thanks all. :pray:

retry-bot: Incident helper: linked runbook -> https://redwood.internal/runbooks/429-burst-handling. Open a follow-up if you want a postmortem template.

alice (Support): Closing loop: customer accepted guidance, applied idempotency keys and reduced retries, they reported no further duplicates. Billing credit issued. Marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
